findings.title: v1/index.m3u8: BANDWIDTH 600 kb/s is 41.9% below the measured peak 1.03 Mb/s
findings.detail: BANDWIDTH 600 kb/s (600000 b/s) is 41.9% below the peak segment bit rate 1.03 Mb/s (887 kb/s the variant's playlist + 145 kb/s its largest audio rendition), segment #1, 2.000 s (1032061 b/s). RFC 8216 §4.3.4.2: BANDWIDTH MUST be the largest sum of peak segment bit rates of any playable combination of renditions; a player that fits BANDWIDTH to its link can stall on this variant.

findings.title: v1/index.m3u8: CODECS names another profile than the stream's
findings.detail: CODECS says H.264 Main, level 3.0 (avc1.4d401e); the stream is H.264 High, level 3.0 (avc1.64001e). Devices choose variants by the profile they can decode.

findings.title: v2/index.m3u8: segment #7 starts with a P/B picture
findings.detail: A player that starts or switches there cannot show anything until the next random access point. One has no random access point at all: #7. EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS says every segment decodes without the ones before it (RFC 8216 §4.3.5.1).

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: CODECS level 3 below the stream's 3.1
findings.detail: CODECS says HEVC Main 10, Main tier, level 3 (hvc1.2.4.L90.B0); the stream is HEVC Main 10, Main tier, level 3.1 (hvc1.2.4.L93.90): a device limited to level 3 can choose a variant it cannot decode.

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: VIDEO-RANGE absent (SDR), the video is PQ
findings.detail: No VIDEO-RANGE, which means SDR, but the video is PQ: 16 (PQ (SMPTE ST 2084)). draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22: VIDEO-RANGE MUST be PQ for transfer 16 and HLG for 18 (also mixed with SDR), SDR for 1, 6, 13, 14, 15; absent means SDR.

findings.title: v1/index.m3u8: AVERAGE-BANDWIDTH -49% off the measured average
findings.detail: AVERAGE-BANDWIDTH 500 kb/s is -49.2% off the average segment bit rate 983 kb/s (840 kb/s + 144 kb/s audio).

findings.title: v1/index.m3u8: FRAME-RATE 30.000, the video is 25.000 fps
findings.detail: FRAME-RATE 30.000; the segments read run at up to 25.000 fps. FRAME-RATE is the maximum frame rate, rounded to three decimal places (RFC 8216 §4.3.4.2).

findings.title: audio "English" (a1/index.m3u8): CHANNELS "6", it decodes to 2 channels
findings.detail: RFC 8216 §4.3.4.1: the first CHANNELS parameter is the largest number of independent, simultaneous channels in any segment of the rendition.

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: RESOLUTION 1920×1080, the video is 1280×720
findings.detail: RESOLUTION 1920×1080 but the video decodes at 1280×720.

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: segment #0's pictures span -0.160 s off its EXTINF
findings.detail: #0 1.840 s against 2.000 s. EXTINF is a segment's duration (RFC 8216 §4.3.2.1): players lay out the timeline, and seek, by it.

findings.title: v2/index.m3u8: BANDWIDTH 1.94 × the measured peak
findings.detail: BANDWIDTH 2.00 Mb/s is 1.94 × the peak segment bit rate 1.03 Mb/s (888 kb/s the variant's playlist + 145 kb/s its largest audio rendition), segment #2, 1.520 s: players wait for a faster link than the variant needs.

findings.title: v2/index.m3u8: segment #4's pictures span -0.080 s off its EXTINF
findings.detail: #4 1.520 s against 1.600 s. The segments have leading pictures (an open GOP, or cuts inside GOPs): the next segment's first pictures show in this one's time, so the spans differ from EXTINF by them.

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: BANDWIDTH 1.67 × the measured peak
findings.detail: BANDWIDTH 4.00 Mb/s is 1.67 × the peak segment bit rate 2.39 Mb/s (2.25 Mb/s the variant's playlist + 145 kb/s its largest audio rendition), segment #1, 2.000 s: players wait for a faster link than the variant needs.

findings.title: v3/index.m3u8: segments start with CRA pictures
findings.detail: #3, 5: clean random access points. The RASL pictures that follow one reference the segment before, and are dropped when playback starts or switches there.
